stem.text: Algae are aquatic photosynthetic protoctists. The alga Alexandrium is red in colour. Alexandrium causes harmful algal blooms (HABs) that turn seawater red when Alexandrium numbers rise to high levels. The abundance of Alexandrium depends mainly on abiotic factors.

Alexandrium releases a toxin that accumulates in shellfish such as oysters and mussels. Humans who eat shellfish contaminated with Alexandrium toxin show signs of poisoning, which in some cases may cause death.
Figure 7.1 shows the global number of cases of poisoning linked to Alexandrium HABs between 1986 and 2018. The line shows the long-term trend in cases of poisoning due to Alexandrium HABs.

stem.caption: Figure 7.1
stem.alt: Cases of poisoning associated with Alexandrium harmful algal blooms from 1986 to 2018 and the long-term trend.

stem.text: Use the long-term trend line shown in Figure 7.1 to calculate the percentage change in cases of poisoning due to Alexandrium HABs between the start of 1986 and the end of 2018.
Show your working and give your answer to three significant figures.

guidance: ECF answer to 3 s.f. from correct working with mis-read graph figures (from bars or trend line)
markScheme.note: Point n follows the order of the transcribed marking points; table rows or source labels such as 3a and 3b retain their original wording.

explanation.text: Percentage change uses the starting trend-line value as its denominator. The stated comparison gives (92 − 35) / 35 × 100, which rounds to 163% to three significant figures. The calculation itself has no syllabus point of its own; it is read here as the data step behind (a)(ii)'s abiotic-factor question, so it shares that point's reference.

reasoningChain: Read both endpoints from the trend line.
Subtract the initial value and divide by that initial value before multiplying by 100.

stem.text: The number of cases of poisoning due to Alexandrium HABs in Figure 7.1 is an indirect measure of the abundance of Alexandrium. Changes in the abundance of Alexandrium can be related to changes in abiotic factors that affect the metabolism, growth and reproduction of the alga.
Identify, with reasons, two abiotic factors that will affect the metabolism of the photosynthetic alga Alexandrium.

explanation.text: Give a factor and a mechanistic reason as a pair. Light affects energy capture, carbon dioxide supplies the Calvin cycle, and temperature affects enzyme-catalysed steps.

reasoningChain: Choose two fully named abiotic factors.

stem.text: The toxin released by Alexandrium is described as a neurotoxin. It binds to, and blocks, voltage-gated sodium ion channels in cell surface membranes of neurones, preventing them from functioning. This results in muscle paralysis because calcium ions are not released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum of muscle cells.
Explain how the action of Alexandrium toxin on a neurone prevents the release of calcium ions from the sarcoplasmic reticulum of muscle cells of a person who has consumed the toxin.

explanation.text: Blocking voltage-gated sodium channels interrupts action-potential propagation. The failure then passes along a causal chain: no terminal depolarisation, no calcium-triggered transmitter release, and no excitation of the muscle membrane.

reasoningChain: Begin with sodium entry into the neurone.
Follow the interruption through the synaptic knob and neuromuscular junction to the muscle.
